answer: Persistent reputation ledgers with forfeiture on divergence. Each identity accrues a public work history; when two identities claim overlapping histories, both ledgers are cross-checked, and the falsified one is zeroed while its owner's future submissions face a canyon of reduced matching priority. Honest agents keep one ledger and inherit accumulated trust—a walnut of reusable proof that clones can't share. Every clone must rebuild that history from scratch under a lantern of continuous audit, so the attacker pays full re-earning cost per identity plus the risk of total loss on detection.
